# Glossary {#sec-glossary .unnumbered}

Terms are collected here from the 'vocabulary of this
chapter' sections, which remain in place: this appendix is a
single alphabetical view of them, not a replacement. Each
entry names the chapter that develops the term, and a term
developed in more than one chapter names each.


## A {.unnumbered}

**Archetype.** The kind of research object a compendium is (data
analysis, manuscript, package, simulation study, or blog), which
varies the layout and the gates but not the underlying
machinery. (@sec-compendium)


## B {.unnumbered}

**Backend.** The mechanism that supplies the environment. Docker
is the container backend; Nix is a container-free backend that
declares the environment directly. (@sec-backends)

**Base image.** The starting image a recipe builds on, named on
the `FROM` line. Here, a Rocker image providing a fixed R
version on a fixed operating system. (@sec-containers)

**Branch.** A movable name for a line of development. The
default branch is conventionally called `main`.
(@sec-version-control)


## C {.unnumbered}

**Capture.** Fixing an input so that it cannot drift: writing a
lockfile, building a container image. Capture sets the
reproducibility level. (@sec-levels)

**Checksum.** A short fingerprint, computed from a file's or an
object's bytes by a hash function such as SHA-256, with the
property that any change to the input, however small, changes
the fingerprint. A stored checksum lets a later run detect that
an input has been altered. (@sec-verification)

**Code chunk.** A block of executable code embedded in a
literate document, delimited from the prose, whose output is
inserted into the rendered document at the chunk's position.
(@sec-literate)

**Commit.** A recorded snapshot of the tracked files at one
moment, carrying an author, a timestamp, a message, and an
immutable identifier (a *hash*). The atomic unit of history.
(@sec-version-control)

**Computational reproducibility.** Obtaining the same numerical
results from the same data and the same code, on another machine
or at a later time. (@sec-crisis)

**Container.** A running instance of an image. One image can
start many containers; each begins from the same frozen
filesystem. (@sec-containers)

**Container image.** A packaged environment, built from a
recipe, that carries the operating system, the system libraries,
and the language runtime, and runs identically wherever a
container runtime runs. (@sec-levels)

**Content hash.** A short fingerprint computed from a package's
contents, so that two installations claiming the same version
can be confirmed byte-identical. (@sec-dependencies)

**Continuous integration (CI).** A hosted service that, on every
committed change to a repository, checks out the code onto a
fresh virtual machine, rebuilds the project, and runs a defined
set of checks, reporting success or failure automatically.
(@sec-verification)


## D {.unnumbered}

**Daemon.** A background system service that runs continuously
with elevated privilege. Docker relies on one; Podman and
Apptainer do not, which is why they run without administrative
rights. (@sec-backends)

**Data-validation test.** A check on the data itself rather than
the code: that a value lies in a plausible range, that no
impossible ages appear, that the expected columns are present.
(@sec-testing)

**Dated snapshot.** A view of a repository frozen as it stood on
a particular calendar day, so that an install run today and one
run next year fetch the same versions. (@sec-dependencies,
@sec-containers)

**Dependency graph.** The graph whose nodes are the steps and
whose edges record that one step consumes what another produces.
A valid pipeline's graph is a *directed acyclic graph* (DAG):
directed because inputs flow to outputs, and acyclic because a
step cannot, directly or transitively, depend on its own output.
(@sec-pipelines)

**Dependency-manifest gate.** A CI check that enforces the
dependency invariant of @sec-dependencies. In its strict,
R-package form it requires every package the code uses to be
declared in `DESCRIPTION` and pinned in `renv.lock`. For a
research compendium, whose `DESCRIPTION` declares only the API
exported from `R/` while analysis scripts legitimately draw on
packages present in `renv.lock` but not in `DESCRIPTION`, it
enforces the weaker inclusion that every package the code uses
is pinned in `renv.lock`. (@sec-verification)

**`DESCRIPTION`.** The human-authored file that declares a
project's direct dependencies by role (`Imports`, `Suggests`,
`Depends`), with optional version floors. (@sec-dependencies)

**Determinant stack.** The layered set of things a computational
result depends upon, from the hardware at the base through the
environment and the packages to the analysis code and the data
at the top. A layer is 'pinned' when it has been fixed to a
recorded value. (@sec-crisis, @sec-levels)

**Determinism (of a render).** The property that rendering the
same source under the same environment produces a byte-for-byte
identical output file. A rendered PDF is usually not
deterministic in this strict sense, for reasons developed below.
(@sec-literate)


## E {.unnumbered}

**Expectation.** A single assertion, such as
`expect_equal(actual, expected)`, that passes or fails.
(@sec-testing)


## F {.unnumbered}

**FAIR.** A set of principles holding that a research object
should be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable,
formulated for data and later adapted for research software.
(@sec-archiving)

**Forge.** A platform that hosts a version-controlled repository
and runs its continuous integration. GitHub and GitLab are the
two principal forges; GitLab is frequently self-hosted by
universities. (@sec-verification, @sec-archiving)


## G {.unnumbered}

**`.gitignore`.** A file listing path patterns that git should
not track, used to keep derived outputs, large data, and,
critically, sensitive files out of the history.
(@sec-version-control)


## I {.unnumbered}

**Image.** A frozen, read-only filesystem together with
metadata, bundling an operating system, R, a set of packages,
and configuration. It is analogous to a snapshot of a fully
installed computer, packaged so it can be shipped.
(@sec-containers)

**Input-addressed.** Identified by a hash of the build inputs
rather than by a mutable name, so that a reference cannot
silently point at different content later. (@sec-backends)

**Integration test.** A check that several components behave
correctly when composed into a pipeline, from raw input to final
result. (@sec-testing)

**Invalidation.** The act of marking a target out of date
because something it depends on, a file, an upstream target, a
function, or a package, has changed. (@sec-pipelines)


## L {.unnumbered}

**Landmine.** A pattern in a document that makes the render
succeed for its author and fail for a later reader, by reaching
outside the captured and committed material. (@sec-literate)

**Layer.** Each instruction in an image's recipe produces one
filesystem layer. An image is the stack of its layers, and
identical layers are shared and cached across images.
(@sec-containers)

**Linting.** Static analysis of source code for stylistic and
likely-error patterns, performed by `lintr`, without running the
code. (@sec-testing)

**Literate programming.** Writing narrative prose and executable
code together in one source document, so the document is at once
the program and its explanation. The term is Knuth's.
(@sec-literate)

**Lockfile.** A machine-generated file, `renv.lock`, recording
the exact version, source repository, and content hash of every
package in a project's library. (@sec-levels, @sec-dependencies)


## O {.unnumbered}

**OCI image.** An image built to the Open Container Initiative
specification, the common format that Docker, Podman, and
Apptainer can all consume. A Docker image is an OCI image.
(@sec-backends)

**OCI tarball or SIF file.** A container image exported as a
single file, checksummable and depositable as an archival
artifact. An OCI image is exported as a tar archive, whereas SIF
is the self-contained single-file format used by the Apptainer
runtime. (@sec-archiving)

**Oracle.** The source of independent truth a test compares
against; the known correct answer. (@sec-testing)


## P {.unnumbered}

**Package churn (code rot).** The gradual breakage of
once-working code as the packages beneath it are updated over
time. (@sec-crisis)

**Package library.** The directory into which R installs
packages. A project-local library belongs to one project rather
than being shared across all of a user's work.
(@sec-dependencies)

**Package repository.** A server, such as CRAN or the Posit
Package Manager, from which packages are installed.
(@sec-dependencies)

**Persistent identifier (DOI).** A durable, resolvable name for
a deposited artifact, such as a Digital Object Identifier, that
continues to resolve even if the artifact moves.
(@sec-archiving)

**Pipeline.** An analysis expressed as a set of steps, each
declaring its inputs and outputs, so that the whole can be
re-executed by a single command that runs the steps in
dependency order. (@sec-pipelines)

**Pre-commit hook.** A script that git runs automatically before
a commit is recorded, used here to run the linter and the styler
as a gate. (@sec-testing)

**Prerequisite.** In Make, an input a target depends on. If any
prerequisite is newer than the target, the target is out of
date. (@sec-pipelines)

**Profile.** The base-image bundle a project is built from, such
as `minimal`, `tidyverse`, `rstudio`, or `publishing`. It
selects the `FROM` image. (@sec-containers)

**Progressive disclosure.** The property that one layout
supports a project's evolution from one archetype to another
with no reorganization. (@sec-compendium)

**Pull request (merge request).** A proposal, made on the
remote, to merge one branch or fork into another, reviewed
before it is accepted. (@sec-version-control)

**Purely functional package manager.** A package manager, such
as Nix, in which the installed result is a deterministic
function of the declared inputs, so that the same declaration
yields a deterministic, reproducible environment.
(@sec-backends)


## R {.unnumbered}

**`R CMD check`.** The standard R command that builds a package,
runs its tests, and applies dozens of standardized checks; here
it serves as a universal integrity gate on the whole compendium.
(@sec-compendium, @sec-verification)

**Raw versus derived data.** Immutable original inputs versus
the processed datasets regenerated from them by code.
(@sec-compendium)

**Recipe (or command).** The shell command Make runs to bring a
target up to date from its prerequisites. (@sec-pipelines)

**Registry.** A server that stores and distributes container
images, from which collaborators pull a pre-built environment.
GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) and Docker Hub are the two in
common use. (@sec-archiving)

**Remote.** A copy of the repository hosted elsewhere, typically
on GitHub or GitLab, used for backup, distribution, and
collaboration. `origin` is the conventional name of the primary
remote. (@sec-version-control)

**Render gate.** A CI check that re-renders the compendium's
report (an R Markdown or Quarto document) from source and fails
the build if the render errors. (@sec-compendium,
@sec-verification)

**Render (verb and noun).** To execute a literate source
document and produce a finished output file (HTML, PDF, Word);
and the resulting file itself. (@sec-literate)

**Rendering toolchain.** The programs a render invokes behind
the scenes: `knitr` or the Quarto engine to run the code,
`pandoc` to convert the result, and, for PDF, a LaTeX
distribution to typeset it. (@sec-literate)

**Replicability.** Obtaining consistent findings from a new
study, with new data, aimed at the same question. (@sec-crisis)

**Repository (repo).** A directory whose contents and full
history git tracks, held in a hidden `.git` subdirectory. A
*clone* is a complete copy of a repository, history and all.
(@sec-version-control)

**Reproduced.** Obtaining the same computational result by
re-executing the same code on the same data. Contrast
**replicated**, obtaining a consistent finding from a new study
with new data. (@sec-levels)

**Reproducibility test.** A check that a recorded computational
result regenerates, either across repeated runs with a fixed
seed or against a stored baseline. (@sec-testing)

**Research compendium.** A single self-describing directory
bundling the code, data, prose, and environment record of an
analysis, organized by convention so that it can be located and
re-run. (@sec-crisis, @sec-compendium)

**Restore.** The reverse act of reading the lockfile and
reinstalling exactly the packages it records.
(@sec-dependencies)

**RNG kind.** The random-number algorithm in force, set by
`RNGkind()`. Two runs with the same seed but a different kind
draw different numbers. (@sec-levels)

**Robustness.** Reaching the same qualitative conclusion from
the same data under different but defensible analytical choices.
(@sec-crisis)

**Rocker.** The community project that publishes the standard R
Docker images. (@sec-containers)

**Rootless.** Able to run under an ordinary user account,
without the `root` superuser privilege. A requirement on shared
clusters, where users are not administrators. (@sec-backends)

**R-package skin.** The minimal set of files (`DESCRIPTION`,
`NAMESPACE`, an `R/` directory) that makes a directory a valid R
package, and therefore checkable by the R build tools.
(@sec-compendium)

**Runner.** The fresh, ephemeral machine (usually a virtual
machine or a container) on which the CI service executes the
workflow. It is discarded after the run, so nothing persists
between runs except what the workflow explicitly restores.
(@sec-verification)

**Runtime.** The program that runs a container image: Docker,
Podman, or Apptainer. The runtime is interchangeable when the
image is a standard OCI image. (@sec-backends)


## S {.unnumbered}

**Sealed render.** A document in which every reported number and
figure is regenerated from the code that produces it on each
build, so the prose cannot drift from the analysis.
(@sec-literate)

**Seed and RNG kind.** The seed (`set.seed`) is the fixed
starting point that makes a random draw repeatable; the RNG kind
is the generator algorithm that turns that seed into numbers,
and its default has changed across R versions. (@sec-crisis)

**SIF.** The Singularity Image Format, a single-file archive
that Apptainer produces from an image, suitable for depositing
alongside a compendium. (@sec-backends)

**Silent default.** A behavior that software applies unless told
otherwise, and that can change between software versions without
any error or warning to the analyst. (@sec-crisis)

**Snapshot.** The act of scanning a project, resolving the
versions currently installed, and writing them into the
lockfile. (@sec-dependencies)

**`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.** A conventional environment variable,
honored by many document tools, that fixes the timestamp a build
embeds, so that two builds do not differ merely because they ran
at different moments. (@sec-literate)

**Staging area (index).** The set of changes marked, with `git
add`, to go into the next commit. Staging lets a commit hold a
chosen subset of the current changes. (@sec-version-control)

**Staleness (out-of-date).** The condition of a target whose
inputs have changed since it was last built, so that its stored
output no longer reflects its inputs. (@sec-pipelines)

**Styling.** Automatic reformatting of source code to a
consistent layout, performed by `styler`. (@sec-testing)


## T {.unnumbered}

**Tag.** A permanent, human-readable name for one specific
commit, used to mark a milestone such as a manuscript
submission. (@sec-version-control)

**Tag and digest.** A tag, such as `rocker/tidyverse:4.4.0`, is
a human-readable pointer that may later be repointed. A digest,
`@sha256:...`, is an immutable hash of the image's exact
content. The same digest always denotes byte-identical bytes.
(@sec-containers)

**Target.** A single step in the pipeline, together with the
output it produces. The word is shared by Make and `targets`,
with a shift of emphasis: for Make a target is a file, for
`targets` it is more often an R object. (@sec-pipelines)

**The Five Pillars.** The five artifacts a compendium manages,
one per capture point: the `Dockerfile`, `renv.lock`,
`.Rprofile`, the source code, and the data. (@sec-compendium)

**The level ladder (L0 to L3).** The four-rung scale, L0
locatable, L1 pinned packages, L2 pinned environment, L3
verified, used throughout this book to grade how far down the
stack an analysis has been secured. (@sec-levels)

**`tinytest`.** A lightweight, zero-dependency R testing
framework in which a test file is a plain script of bare,
top-level expectation calls [@vanderloo2020]. (@sec-testing)

**Two-layer team model.** A division of a project into a
slow-moving environment layer, fixed once by a team lead, and a
fast-moving package layer, extended by every contributor.
(@sec-archiving)


## U {.unnumbered}

**Union model.** The rule that the project lockfile records the
union of every package any contributor has installed, so that a
rebuilt image carries what the whole team needs, not only what
one member used. (@sec-archiving)

**Unit test.** A focused check that one small piece of code,
typically a single function, behaves as intended on known
inputs. (@sec-testing)

**Up-to-date (skippable).** The condition of a target whose
inputs have not changed since it was last built, so that
rebuilding it would reproduce the stored output and can be
skipped. (@sec-pipelines)


## V {.unnumbered}

**Validation.** Confirming that the captured inputs actually
suffice, by rebuilding and re-running. Validation does not pin
anything new; it checks. (@sec-levels)

**Verification.** The act of rebuilding the compendium,
re-running the analysis, and comparing the regenerated
computational outputs against a recorded baseline; passing it is
what the ladder calls level L3. (@sec-verification)


## W {.unnumbered}

**Workflow.** The file, written in YAML, that tells the CI
service what to do: which events trigger it, what environment to
run in, and what commands to execute. On GitHub these files live
under `.github/workflows/`; on GitLab the single file is
`.gitlab-ci.yml`. (@sec-verification)

**Working tree.** The ordinary files in the repository directory
as they currently exist on disk, as opposed to the versions
recorded in the history. (@sec-version-control)


## Z {.unnumbered}

**Zenodo.** A general-purpose research repository, operated at
CERN, that mints a DOI for any deposited file set.
(@sec-archiving)
